lessons.title: Carton erectors and setting up
lessons.html:
Why cartons matter

A fruit carton must survive cold storage at high humidity, stacking two metres high on a pallet, rough handling and weeks at sea. A carton that is badly folded or glued can collapse, crushing the fruit and toppling the pallet. The carton assembly machine (carton erector) forms flat corrugated blanks into strong, square cartons at high speed for the packing line.

Main parts of a carton erector

PartFunction
Blank magazineHolds the stack of flat carton blanks
Feeder (vacuum cups or pick-off)Takes one blank at a time into the machine
Glue system (hot-melt or cold glue)Applies glue to the flaps in set positions
Forming head / mandrel and diePushes the blank through the forming box to fold walls and corners
Compression sectionHolds glued joints until they set
Discharge conveyorCarries formed cartons to the packing area
Control panel and sensorsStart, stop, speed, counters and fault indicators

Setting up for a carton type

Each carton type (for example a citrus, pome fruit or grape carton) may need a changeover of the forming head and guides. Follow the changeover procedure and the settings sheet for that carton.

  1. Confirm the carton type and quantity needed with the packing supervisor.
  2. Check that the blanks are the correct type and print, dry, flat and undamaged. Damp or warped blanks jam and form poorly.
  3. Isolate and lock out the machine before changing tooling or adjusting guides.
  4. Fit the correct forming head and adjust magazine guides to the blank size.
  5. Fill the glue tank with the approved glue. Allow hot-melt units to reach the set temperature.
  6. Check guards, interlocks and emergency stops.
  7. Remove your lock, warn people, and run test cartons at low speed.

lessons.title: Running, quality checks and safety
lessons.html:
Quality checks on formed cartons

Inspect the first cartons after setup and then at regular intervals.

  • Square: walls at right angles and corners tight, without gaps.
  • Glue: correct amount and position. Pull a flap to check the bond: fibres should tear rather than the glue simply letting go. Too much glue is wasteful and can soil the carton.
  • No damage: no crushed corners, torn flaps or scuffed print.
  • Dimensions: cartons must fit the pallet pattern and lids.

Record checks and reject faulty cartons. If faults repeat, stop and find the cause.

Common faults and causes

FaultPossible causes
Blanks not feeding or double feedMagazine guides wrong, worn vacuum cups, warped blanks
Weak or open glue jointsGlue too cold, nozzle blocked, too little glue, dusty or damp blanks
Cartons out of squareWrong forming head setting, worn parts, blank scoring off
Jams at dischargeConveyor backing up, cartons not removed fast enough

Running the machine

  • Keep the magazine topped up so feeding stays even.
  • Match machine speed to the packing line demand to avoid build-up.
  • Keep glue nozzles clean, and refill glue before it runs out.
  • Keep the area tidy: flatten and remove scrap blanks.

Safety

  • The forming head moves with great force and can crush hands. Never bypass guards or interlocks.
  • Stop and lock out before clearing jams, cleaning or adjusting inside guards.
  • Hot-melt glue and nozzles can cause serious burns. Wear the required gloves and safety glasses. If molten glue touches skin, cool it under cold running water for a long time, do not peel it off, and get first aid.
  • Keep loose clothing and hair away from moving parts.
  • Lift blank bundles correctly or use a pallet jack.

End of shift

Run out remaining blanks if instructed, switch off as per procedure, clean glue residue and dust, report wear and faults, and complete the production record with cartons made, rejects and downtime.

Key points

  • Cartons must be square, well glued and undamaged to protect fruit.
  • Use the correct blanks and settings for each carton type.
  • Check first-off and regular cartons; record and reject faults.
  • Lock out before changeovers, jams or cleaning.
  • Protect yourself from crush points and hot glue burns.
